authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: Don't force Bracket 5 with a generic Grixis Oracle/Breach shell (decisions L18).
Underworld Breach and Brain Freeze were cut for identity, not because they don't work (decisions L70).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Mishra must survive to your own combat; sorcery-speed removal or a board wipe resets the engine.
Artifact hate stops copy targets and combos.
A five-mana commander that triggers at combat is slow against cEDH tables.

value.interaction: Force of Will, Mana Drain, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Chaos Warp, Cyclonic Rift, Toxic Deluge.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Mishra is the copy engine and part of most of the deck's infinites.
accepted_role.honest_note: Commander-native: 9 of the 19 Spellbook combos in the list include Mishra, including every infinite-turn line. The engine is a five-mana sorcery-speed combat trigger, which keeps the deck below cEDH speed; the source declined to swap in Oracle/Breach to force Bracket 5. The cycle 51 M1 review (mishraeo-01..09, all verified) confirms the Warform rules and combos.
